559	    /// G-45 (d): This Project first, only when `project` holds an item, with
560	    /// (e)'s duplicate titles told apart; then the templates' categories by
561	    /// case-insensitive name, Other last. Items by title case-insensitively,
562	    /// then by name.
563	    static func categories(
564	        templates: [GraphicBrowserItem], project: [GraphicBrowserItem]
565	    ) -> [GraphicBrowserCategory] {
566	        let ours: [GraphicBrowserCategory] = project.isEmpty ? []
567	            : [GraphicBrowserCategory(name: thisProject, items: sorted(distinguished(project)))]
568	        let names = Set(templates.map(\.category)).sorted { a, b in
569	            if (a == other) != (b == other) { return b == other }
570	            return a.caseInsensitiveCompare(b) == .orderedAscending
571	        }
572	        let theirs = names.map { name in
573	            GraphicBrowserCategory(
574	                name: name, items: sorted(templates.filter { $0.category == name }))
575	        }
576	        return ours + theirs
577	    }

580	    /// `graphics/` holds as the registry compiled them. Main.
581	    static func categories(for document: ProjectDocument) -> [GraphicBrowserCategory] {
582	        let templates = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entries.map {
583	            item(name: $0.template.name, entry: $0.entry, origin: .template)
584	        }
585	        let modules = document.graphicStore?.scan.modules.keys.sorted() ?? []

594	    /// By title, case-insensitively, then by name.
595	    private static func sorted(_ items: [GraphicBrowserItem]) -> [GraphicBrowserItem] {
596	        items.sorted { a, b in
597	            switch a.title.caseInsensitiveCompare(b.title) {
598	            case .orderedAscending: return true
599	            case .orderedDescending: return false
600	            case .orderedSame: return a.name < b.name
601	            }
602	        }
603	    }

605	    /// Every item whose title another item shares, case-insensitively,
606	    /// titled "<title> — <name>".
607	    private static func distinguished(_ items: [GraphicBrowserItem]) -> [GraphicBrowserItem] {
608	        var counts: [String: Int] = [:]
609	        let key = { (title: String) in title.folding(options: .caseInsensitive, locale: nil) }
610	        for item in items { counts[key(item.title), default: 0] += 1 }
611	        return items.map { item in
612	            guard counts[key(item.title), default: 0] > 1 else { return item }
613	            return GraphicBrowserItem(
614	                name: item.name, title: "\(item.title) — \(item.name)",
615	                description: item.description, category: item.category, origin: item.origin,
616	                ok: item.ok)
617	        }
618	    }

621	/// The bundled templates, compiled once against a library of the bundled
622	/// fonts (G-45 (e)): what the browser reads their `meta` from and what its
623	/// preview draws them with.
624	final class GraphicTemplateLibrary {
625	    struct Entry {
626	        let template: GraphicTemplate
627	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry
628	    }
629	
630	    static let shared = GraphicTemplateLibrary(
631	        directory: GraphicTemplates.bundledDirectory, fonts: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory)
632	
633	    private let directory: URL
634	    private let fonts: URL
635	    private let lock = NSLock()
636	    private var compiled: [Entry]?
637	
638	    init(directory: URL, fonts: URL) {
639	        self.directory = directory
640	        self.fonts = fonts
641	    }
642	
643	    /// Every template in `GraphicTemplates.list(in:)`'s order, compiled on
644	    /// the first read and kept. The first read is on main.
645	    var entries: [Entry] {
646	        lock.lock()
647	        defer { lock.unlock() }
648	        if let compiled = compiled { return compiled }
649	        let made = compile()
650	        compiled = made
651	        return made
652	    }
653	
654	    func entry(named name: String) -> Entry? {
655	        entries.first { $0.template.name == name }
656	    }
657	
658	    /// The bundled faces into a new library, then every template compiled
659	    /// against it. A face the engine refuses fails every template with its
660	    /// sentence, as `GraphicRegistry.install` does for a document.
661	    private func compile() -> [Entry] {
662	        let templates = GraphicTemplates.list(in: directory)
663	        let library = GraphicLibrary()
664	        var refused: [GraphicDiagnostic]?
665	        let faces = ((try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
666	            at: fonts, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil)) ?? [])
667	            .filter { GraphicStore.fontExtensions.contains($0.pathExtension.lowercased()) }
668	            .sorted { $0.lastPathComponent < $1.lastPathComponent }
669	        do {
670	            for face in faces { try library.addFont(Data(contentsOf: face)) }
671	        } catch {
672	            refused = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
673	        }
674	        return templates.map { template in
675	            let bytes = (try? Data(contentsOf: template.url)) ?? Data()
676	            if let refused = refused {
677	                return Entry(template: template, entry: .failed(refused, revision: ""))
678	            }
679	            let file = GraphicModuleFile(
680	                name: template.name, url: template.url, bytes: bytes, revision: "")
681	            return Entry(template: template, entry: GraphicRegistry.compile(file, library: library))
682	        }
683	    }
684	}

899	extension ProjectDocument {
900	    /// The sentence for a document whose graphics store has not started —

905	    /// Writes `url`'s module into `graphics/` under a free name made from
906	    /// its stem (G-16 (b)) and rescans; the name it was written under.
907	    /// Throws, writing nothing, when the file cannot be read or is not
908	    /// UTF-8.
909	    func writeGraphicModule(from url: URL) throws -> String {
910	        guard let store = graphicStore else {
911	            throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
912	        }
913	        let bytes: Data
914	        do {
915	            bytes = try Data(contentsOf: url)
916	        } catch {
917	            throw ReelCoreError(
918	                message: "\(url.path) could not be read: \(error.localizedDescription)")
919	        }
920	        guard let source = String(data: bytes, encoding: .utf8) else {
921	            throw ReelCoreError(
922	                message: "\(url.path) is not UTF-8 text — a graphic module must be UTF-8 "
923	                    + "JavaScript")
924	        }
925	        let name = store.uniqueModuleName(
926	            GraphicTemplates.moduleName(from: url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent))
927	        try store.write(name: name, source: source)
928	        store.rescan()
929	        return name
930	    }

933	    /// and a time: its `meta` duration and size, its schema. Throws the
934	    /// module's first diagnostic when it does not compile, the store's
935	    /// sentence when the folder does not hold it, and the `meta` sentence
936	    /// when a duration or side is not a whole number in range.
937	    func graphicClipMaker(named name: String) throws -> (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp {
938	        guard let store = graphicStore else {
939	            throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
940	        }
941	        guard let entry = GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: name, for: recipeKey) else {
942	            throw ReelCoreError(message: store.noModuleSentence(name))
943	        }
944	        guard case .compiled(_, _, let meta, let schema) = entry else {
945	            var first: GraphicDiagnostic?
946	            if case .failed(let diagnostics, _) = entry { first = diagnostics.first }
947	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""
948	            throw ReelCoreError(
949	                message: "graphics/\(name).js does not compile: "
950	                    + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic") + line)
951	        }
952	        let frame = max(project.snapshot.canvas.fps.frameDuration, 1)
953	        let duration: Ticks?
954	        let width: UInt32?
955	        let height: UInt32?
956	        do {
957	            duration = try AgentServer.metaWhole(
958	                meta, "durationInFrames", name, in: 1...Int.max / Int(frame)
959	            ).map { Ticks($0) * frame }
960	            width = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "width", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
961	                .map(UInt32.init)
962	            height = try AgentServer.metaWhole(meta, "height", name, in: AgentServer.sides)
963	                .map(UInt32.init)
964	        } catch let error as AgentServer.ToolError {
965	            throw ReelCoreError(message: error.message)
966	        }
967	        return { track, at in
968	            .addGraphicClipRaw(
969	                track: track, at: at, duration: duration, name: name, width: width,
970	                height: height, props: nil, schema: schema)
971	        }
972	    }

1	// app/Sources/GraphicBrowserSheetController.swift — Insert ▸ Graphic… (spec
2	// §11 G-45): a sheet of three panes — the categories, the graphics of the
3	// chosen one, and a looping preview of the chosen graphic with its title and
4	// one-line description — over a message line and a bottom bar of Export… and
5	// From File… at the left and Cancel and Insert at the right.
6	//
7	// **What it lists is `GraphicCatalog.categories(for:)`**, read once when the
8	// sheet is made, in the order `list_graphics` answers. It opens on the first
9	// category's first graphic; Insert is disabled with no graphic chosen, and a
10	// double-click on a graphic is Insert.
11	//
12	// **No second implementation.** Insert is one call of the editor's body —
13	// `insertGraphic(from:grouped:)` with the template's URL, or
14	// `insertProjectGraphic(named:grouped:)` for This Project — the bodies the
15	// old menu items called, which call `ProjectDocument+GraphicInsert.swift`
16	// as `insert_graphic` does. It runs inside the button's event, so `grouped:
17	// false` (`applyEdit`). A success dismisses the sheet; a throw beeps and
18	// shows the sentence word for word in `messageLabel`, and the sheet stays.
19	//
20	// **What follows the sheet starts in `viewDidDisappear`**, for
21	// `ReverseProgressSheetController`'s reason: a sheet dismissed a moment ago
22	// is still the window's `attachedSheet`. From File… only sets a flag and
23	// dismisses; the open panel is begun there, once the browser is down. And
24	// the preview's render thread is stopped there, so every way out — Cancel,
25	// Esc, Insert, From File… — stops it.
26	//
27	// **Opened after an import** (spec §11 G-47 (f)) with `select`: This Project
28	// and the graphic of that name are chosen, and `message` is put in the
29	// message line after the choice has cleared it.
30	//
31	// **Export…** (spec §11 G-46 (a)) is enabled when the chosen graphic
32	// compiles and no export is running. It opens a save panel as a sheet on the
33	// browser, which stays up; `exportChosen(to:)` builds a `GraphicPackageJob` on
34	// main and writes it on a `Thread` of `GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes`
35	// (QuickJS needs the stack), and the result or the refusal goes in the
36	// message line. No edit and no undo step.
37	
38	import AppKit
39	
40	final class GraphicBrowserSheetController: NSViewController, NSTableViewDataSource,
41	    NSTableViewDelegate

43	    /// Weak, like every sheet's back-reference.

49	    /// The graphic to choose and the message to show at load (G-47 (f)).
50	    private let select: String?

52	    /// An export's thread is running; Export… stays disabled until it reports.
53	    private(set) var exporting = false
54	    /// The last export's thread, for the probe to see it finish.
55	    private(set) var exportThread: Thread?
56	
57	    private let categoryTable = NSTableView()
58	    private let graphicTable = NSTableView()
59	    private let previewView = NSImageView()
60	    private let titleLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
61	    private let descriptionLabel = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
62	    private let messageLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
63	    private let insertButton: NSButton
64	    private let fromFileButton: NSButton
65	    private let exportButton: NSButton

67	    /// The preview's loop; its thread starts with the first graphic shown.
68	    private(set) lazy var player = GraphicPreviewPlayer(canvas: canvas) { [weak self] image in
69	        self?.showFrame(image)
70	    }

73	    private static let paneHeight: CGFloat = 410
74	    private static let categoriesWidth: CGFloat = 180
75	    private static let graphicsWidth: CGFloat = 240

81	        message: String? = nil

105	        let contentWidth = Self.width - sheetInset * 2
106	        let previewWidth = contentWidth - Self.categoriesWidth - Self.graphicsWidth - Self.gap * 2

116	        let aspect = CGFloat(max(canvas.width, 1)) / CGFloat(max(canvas.height, 1))
117	        let well = aspect >= room.width / room.height
118	            ? NSSize(width: room.width, height: (room.width / aspect).rounded())
119	            : NSSize(width: (room.height * aspect).rounded(), height: room.height)
120	        previewView.imageScaling = .scaleProportionallyUpOrDown
121	        previewView.wantsLayer = true
122	        previewView.layer?.backgroundColor = DS.canvasVoid.cgColor
123	        previewView.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.preview")
124	        previewView.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
125	        previewView.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: well.width).isActive = true
126	        previewView.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: well.height).isActive = true
127	
128	        titleLabel.font = DS.sans(13, weight: .bold)
129	        titleLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
130	        titleLabel.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
131	        titleLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.title")
132	        descriptionLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
133	        descriptionLabel.textColor = DS.textMuted
134	        descriptionLabel.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
135	        descriptionLabel.maximumNumberOfLines = 1
136	        descriptionLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.description")
137	        // A plain view with every edge pinned, so nothing in the column is
138	        // left to a stack's low-priority guesses.
139	        let previewColumn = NSView()
140	        previewColumn.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
141	        for label in [titleLabel, descriptionLabel] {
142	            label.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
143	            label.setContentCompressionResistancePriority(.defaultLow, for: .horizontal)
144	        }
145	        for piece in [previewView, titleLabel, descriptionLabel] { previewColumn.addSubview(piece) }
146	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
147	            previewColumn.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: previewWidth),
148	            previewColumn.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight),
149	            previewView.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.topAnchor),
150	            previewView.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.leadingAnchor),
151	            titleLabel.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewView.bottomAnchor, constant: 10),
152	            descriptionLabel.topAnchor.constraint(equalTo: titleLabel.bottomAnchor, constant: 6),
153	        ] + [titleLabel, descriptionLabel].flatMap { label in
154	            [
155	                label.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: previewColumn.leadingAnchor),
156	                label.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: previewWidth),
157	            ]
158	        })
159	
160	        let panes = NSStackView(views: [
161	            scroll(categoryTable, width: Self.categoriesWidth),
162	            scroll(graphicTable, width: Self.graphicsWidth), previewColumn,
163	        ])
164	        panes.orientation = .horizontal
165	        panes.alignment = .top
166	        panes.spacing = Self.gap
167	        panes.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight).isActive = true
168	
169	        messageLabel.font = DS.sans(12)
170	        messageLabel.textColor = DS.textStrong
171	        messageLabel.preferredMaxLayoutWidth = contentWidth
172	        messageLabel.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.message")
173	
174	        insertButton.target = self
175	        insertButton.action = #selector(insertClicked(_:))
176	        insertButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.insert")
177	        fromFileButton.target = self
178	        fromFileButton.action = #selector(fromFileClicked(_:))
179	        fromFileButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.fromFile")
180	        exportButton.target = self
181	        exportButton.action = #selector(exportClicked(_:))
182	        exportButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.export")
183	        let cancelButton = sheetCancelButton(target: self, action: #selector(cancelClicked(_:)))
184	        cancelButton.setAccessibilityIdentifier("graphicbrowser.cancel")
185	        view = makeSheetView(
186	            title: "Insert Graphic", content: sheetColumn([panes, messageLabel]),
187	            buttonRow: makeButtonRow(
188	                cancel: cancelButton, apply: insertButton, leading: [exportButton, fromFileButton]),
189	            width: Self.width)
190	
191	        categoryTable.reloadData()
192	        if !categories.isEmpty {
193	            categoryTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: 0), byExtendingSelection: false)
194	        }
195	        categoryChanged()
196	        chooseSelected()
197	    }
198	
199	    /// `select` chosen under This Project, then `message` shown (G-47 (f)).
200	    private func chooseSelected() {
201	        if let select = select,
202	            let section = categories.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == GraphicCatalog.thisProject }),
203	            let row = categories[section].items.firstIndex(where: { $0.name == select })
204	        {
205	            categoryTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: section), byExtendingSelection: false)
206	            categoryChanged()
207	            graphicTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: row), byExtendingSelection: false)
208	            graphicChanged()
209	        }
210	        if let message = message { messageLabel.stringValue = message }
211	    }
212	
213	    private func configure(_ table: NSTableView, id: String) {
214	        let column = NSTableColumn(identifier: NSUserInterfaceItemIdentifier("name"))
215	        column.resizingMask = .autoresizingMask
216	        table.addTableColumn(column)
217	        table.headerView = nil
218	        table.rowHeight = 24
219	        table.style = .plain
220	        table.focusRingType = .none
221	        table.columnAutoresizingStyle = .firstColumnOnlyAutoresizingStyle
222	        table.dataSource = self
223	        table.delegate = self
224	        table.setAccessibilityIdentifier(id)
225	    }
226	
227	    private func scroll(_ table: NSTableView, width: CGFloat) -> NSScrollView {
228	        let scroll = NSScrollView()
229	        scroll.documentView = table
230	        scroll.hasVerticalScroller = true
231	        scroll.autohidesScrollers = true
232	        scroll.borderType = .lineBorder
233	        scroll.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
234	        scroll.widthAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: width).isActive = true
235	        scroll.heightAnchor.constraint(equalToConstant: Self.paneHeight).isActive = true
236	        table.sizeLastColumnToFit()
237	        return scroll
238	    }
239	
240	    // MARK: - The two lists
241	
242	    private var chosenCategory: GraphicBrowserCategory? {
243	        let row = categoryTable.selectedRow
244	        return categories.indices.contains(row) ? categories[row] : nil
245	    }
246	
247	    private var chosenItem: GraphicBrowserItem? {
248	        let items = chosenCategory?.items ?? []
249	        let row = graphicTable.selectedRow
250	        return items.indices.contains(row) ? items[row] : nil
251	    }
252	
253	    func numberOfRows(in tableView: NSTableView) -> Int {
254	        tableView === categoryTable ? categories.count : (chosenCategory?.items.count ?? 0)
255	    }
256	
257	    func tableView(
258	        _ tableView: NSTableView, viewFor tableColumn: NSTableColumn?, row: Int
259	    ) -> NSView? {
260	        let cell = (tableView.makeView(withIdentifier: Self.cellID, owner: self)
261	            as? NSTableCellView) ?? Self.makeCell()
262	        if tableView === categoryTable {
263	            cell.textField?.stringValue = categories.indices.contains(row)
264	                ? categories[row].name : ""
265	            cell.textField?.textColor = DS.textStrong
266	        } else {
267	            let items = chosenCategory?.items ?? []
268	            let item = items.indices.contains(row) ? items[row] : nil
269	            cell.textField?.stringValue = item?.title ?? ""
270	            cell.textField?.textColor = item?.ok == false ? DS.textFaint : DS.textStrong
271	        }
272	        return cell
273	    }
274	
275	    func tableViewSelectionDidChange(_ notification: Notification) {
276	        if notification.object as? NSTableView === categoryTable {
277	            categoryChanged()
278	        } else {
279	            graphicChanged()
280	        }
281	    }
282	
283	    private static func makeCell() -> NSTableCellView {
284	        let cell = NSTableCellView()
285	        cell.identifier = cellID
286	        let field = NSTextField(labelWithString: "")
287	        field.font = DS.sans(13)
288	        field.lineBreakMode = .byTruncatingTail
289	        field.translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false
290	        cell.addSubview(field)
291	        cell.textField = field
292	        NSLayoutConstraint.activate([
293	            field.leadingAnchor.constraint(equalTo: cell.leadingAnchor, constant: 6),
294	            field.trailingAnchor.constraint(lessThanOrEqualTo: cell.trailingAnchor, constant: -6),
295	            field.centerYAnchor.constraint(equalTo: cell.centerYAnchor),
296	        ])
297	        return cell
298	    }

300	    /// A new category: its graphics listed, the first chosen.
301	    private func categoryChanged() {
302	        graphicTable.reloadData()
303	        if graphicTable.numberOfRows > 0 {
304	            graphicTable.selectRowIndexes(IndexSet(integer: 0), byExtendingSelection: false)
305	        }

309	    /// A new graphic (or none): its title and description, Insert, and the
310	    /// preview playing it.
311	    private func graphicChanged() {
312	        let item = chosenItem
313	        titleLabel.stringValue = item?.title ?? ""
314	        descriptionLabel.stringValue = item?.description ?? ""

323	    /// What the preview draws `item` with: the template library's compile,
324	    /// or the document's registry for This Project.
325	    private func subject(for item: GraphicBrowserItem) -> GraphicPreviewPlayer.Subject {
326	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry?
327	        switch item.origin {
328	        case .template:
329	            entry = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: item.name)?.entry
330	        case .project:
331	            entry = document.flatMap {
332	                GraphicRegistry.shared.entry(named: item.name, for: $0.recipeKey)
333	            }
334	        }
335	        switch entry {
336	        case .compiled(let module, _, let meta, _)?:
337	            return .module(module, name: item.name, meta: meta)
338	        case .failed(let diagnostics, _)?:
339	            return .failed(name: item.name, diagnostics)
340	        case nil:
341	            return .failed(
342	                name: item.name, [.error("graphics/\(item.name).js is not compiled")])
343	        }
344	    }

346	    private func showFrame(_ image: CGImage) {

367	    /// The chosen graphic placed, once. A throw beeps and shows its sentence,
368	    /// and the sheet stays up; a success closes it.
369	    @objc private func insertClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
370	        guard let editor = editor, let item = chosenItem else {
371	            NSSound.beep()
372	            return
373	        }
374	        do {
375	            switch item.origin {
376	            case .template:
377	                guard let template = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: item.name) else {
378	                    throw ReelCoreError(
379	                        message: "The template \"\(item.name)\" is not in this build's bundle")
380	                }
381	                try editor.insertGraphic(from: template.template.url, grouped: false)
382	            case .project:
383	                try editor.insertProjectGraphic(named: item.name, grouped: false)
384	            }
385	        } catch {
386	            NSSound.beep()
387	            messageLabel.stringValue = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message
388	                ?? error.localizedDescription
389	            return
390	        }

394	    // MARK: - Export
395	
396	    /// The save panel, as a sheet on the browser, named `<module>.fjgraphic`.
397	    @objc private func exportClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
398	        guard let item = chosenItem, item.ok, !exporting, let window = view.window else {
399	            NSSound.beep()
400	            return
401	        }
402	        let panel = NSSavePanel()
403	        panel.allowedContentTypes = [GraphicPackage.contentType]
404	        panel.nameFieldStringValue = "\(item.name).\(GraphicPackage.fileExtension)"
405	        panel.beginSheetModal(for: window) { [weak self] response in
406	            guard response == .OK, let url = panel.url else { return }
407	            self?.exportChosen(to: url)
408	        }

411	    /// The panel's OK (and the probe's entry): the chosen graphic's job built here, on main,
412	    /// and written on its own thread. A throw beeps and shows the sentence.
413	    func exportChosen(to url: URL) {
414	        guard let item = chosenItem, let document = document, !exporting else {
415	            NSSound.beep()
416	            return
417	        }
418	        let job: GraphicPackageJob
419	        do {
420	            switch item.origin {
421	            case .template:
422	                guard let template = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entry(named: item.name) else {
423	                    throw ReelCoreError(
424	                        message: "The template \"\(item.name)\" is not in this build's bundle")
425	                }
426	                job = try GraphicPackageJob.template(template, document: document)
427	            case .project:
428	                job = try GraphicPackageJob.project(named: item.name, document: document)
429	            }
430	        } catch {
431	            NSSound.beep()
432	            messageLabel.stringValue = Self.sentence(error)
433	            return
434	        }
435	        exporting = true
436	        exportButton.isEnabled = false
437	        messageLabel.stringValue = "Exporting \(job.title)…"
438	        let thread = Thread { [weak self] in
439	            let outcome = Result { try job.write(to: url) }
440	            DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in self?.exportFinished(job, outcome) }
441	        }
442	        thread.stackSize = GraphicPrefetch.workerStackBytes
443	        thread.name = "com.kgalligan.framejob.graphic-export"
444	        exportThread = thread
445	        thread.start()
446	    }

448	    private func exportFinished(
449	        _ job: GraphicPackageJob, _ outcome: Result<GraphicPackageResult, Error>
450	    ) {
451	        exporting = false
452	        exportButton.isEnabled = chosenItem?.ok == true
453	        switch outcome {
454	        case .success(let result):
455	            messageLabel.stringValue = "Exported \(job.title) to \(result.url.lastPathComponent): "
456	                + result.files.joined(separator: ", ") + "."
457	        case .failure(let error):
458	            NSSound.beep()
459	            messageLabel.stringValue = Self.sentence(error)
460	        }
461	    }

463	    private static func sentence(_ error: Error) -> String {
464	        (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
465	    }

518	enum GraphicCatalog {
519	    static let thisProject = "This Project", other = "Other"
520	
521	    /// G-45 (a): `meta.category` trimmed when it is a non-empty string, else
522	    /// "Other".
523	    static func category(meta: [String: Any]) -> String {
524	        let named = (meta["category"] as? String)?
525	            .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
526	        return named.isEmpty ? other : named
527	    }

529	    /// G-45 (e): `meta.name` when it is a non-empty string, else the stem's
530	    /// title (`GraphicTemplates.title(for:)`).
531	    static func title(meta: [String: Any], name: String) -> String {
532	        let named = (meta["name"] as? String)?
533	            .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""
534	        return named.isEmpty ? GraphicTemplates.title(for: name) : named
535	    }
536	
537	    /// `meta.description` trimmed, nil when absent or blank.
538	    static func description(meta: [String: Any]) -> String? {
539	        let text = (meta["description"] as? String)?
540	            .trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines) ?? ""

544	    /// One item from a compiled (or failed, or absent) registry entry.
545	    static func item(
546	        name: String, entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry?, origin: GraphicBrowserItem.Origin
547	    ) -> GraphicBrowserItem {
548	        var meta: [String: Any] = [:]
549	        var ok = false
550	        if case .compiled(_, _, let described, _)? = entry {
551	            meta = described
552	            ok = true
553	        }
554	        return GraphicBrowserItem(
555	            name: name, title: title(meta: meta, name: name), description: description(meta: meta),
556	            category: category(meta: meta), origin: origin, ok: ok)

559	    /// G-45 (d): This Project first, only when `project` holds an item, with
560	    /// (e)'s duplicate titles told apart; then the templates' categories by
561	    /// case-insensitive name, Other last. Items by title case-insensitively,
562	    /// then by name.
563	    static func categories(
564	        templates: [GraphicBrowserItem], project: [GraphicBrowserItem]
565	    ) -> [GraphicBrowserCategory] {
566	        let ours: [GraphicBrowserCategory] = project.isEmpty ? []
567	            : [GraphicBrowserCategory(name: thisProject, items: sorted(distinguished(project)))]
568	        let names = Set(templates.map(\.category)).sorted { a, b in
569	            if (a == other) != (b == other) { return b == other }
570	            return a.caseInsensitiveCompare(b) == .orderedAscending
571	        }
572	        let theirs = names.map { name in
573	            GraphicBrowserCategory(
574	                name: name, items: sorted(templates.filter { $0.category == name }))
575	        }
576	        return ours + theirs
577	    }

580	    /// `graphics/` holds as the registry compiled them. Main.
581	    static func categories(for document: ProjectDocument) -> [GraphicBrowserCategory] {
582	        let templates = GraphicTemplateLibrary.shared.entries.map {
583	            item(name: $0.template.name, entry: $0.entry, origin: .template)
584	        }
585	        let modules = document.graphicStore?.scan.modules.keys.sorted() ?? []

594	    /// By title, case-insensitively, then by name.
595	    private static func sorted(_ items: [GraphicBrowserItem]) -> [GraphicBrowserItem] {
596	        items.sorted { a, b in
597	            switch a.title.caseInsensitiveCompare(b.title) {
598	            case .orderedAscending: return true
599	            case .orderedDescending: return false
600	            case .orderedSame: return a.name < b.name
601	            }
602	        }
603	    }

605	    /// Every item whose title another item shares, case-insensitively,
606	    /// titled "<title> — <name>".
607	    private static func distinguished(_ items: [GraphicBrowserItem]) -> [GraphicBrowserItem] {
608	        var counts: [String: Int] = [:]
609	        let key = { (title: String) in title.folding(options: .caseInsensitive, locale: nil) }
610	        for item in items { counts[key(item.title), default: 0] += 1 }
611	        return items.map { item in
612	            guard counts[key(item.title), default: 0] > 1 else { return item }
613	            return GraphicBrowserItem(
614	                name: item.name, title: "\(item.title) — \(item.name)",
615	                description: item.description, category: item.category, origin: item.origin,
616	                ok: item.ok)

621	/// The bundled templates, compiled once against a library of the bundled
622	/// fonts (G-45 (e)): what the browser reads their `meta` from and what its
623	/// preview draws them with.
624	final class GraphicTemplateLibrary {
625	    struct Entry {
626	        let template: GraphicTemplate
627	        let entry: GraphicRegistry.Entry
628	    }
629	
630	    static let shared = GraphicTemplateLibrary(
631	        directory: GraphicTemplates.bundledDirectory, fonts: ProjectDocument.bundledFontsDirectory)
632	
633	    private let directory: URL
634	    private let fonts: URL
635	    private let lock = NSLock()
636	    private var compiled: [Entry]?
637	
638	    init(directory: URL, fonts: URL) {
639	        self.directory = directory
640	        self.fonts = fonts
641	    }
642	
643	    /// Every template in `GraphicTemplates.list(in:)`'s order, compiled on
644	    /// the first read and kept. The first read is on main.
645	    var entries: [Entry] {
646	        lock.lock()
647	        defer { lock.unlock() }
648	        if let compiled = compiled { return compiled }
649	        let made = compile()
650	        compiled = made
651	        return made
652	    }
653	
654	    func entry(named name: String) -> Entry? {
655	        entries.first { $0.template.name == name }
656	    }
657	
658	    /// The bundled faces into a new library, then every template compiled
659	    /// against it. A face the engine refuses fails every template with its
660	    /// sentence, as `GraphicRegistry.install` does for a document.
661	    private func compile() -> [Entry] {
662	        let templates = GraphicTemplates.list(in: directory)
663	        let library = GraphicLibrary()
664	        var refused: [GraphicDiagnostic]?
665	        let faces = ((try? FileManager.default.contentsOfDirectory(
666	            at: fonts, includingPropertiesForKeys: nil)) ?? [])
667	            .filter { GraphicStore.fontExtensions.contains($0.pathExtension.lowercased()) }
668	            .sorted { $0.lastPathComponent < $1.lastPathComponent }
669	        do {
670	            for face in faces { try library.addFont(Data(contentsOf: face)) }
671	        } catch {
672	            refused = GraphicDiagnostic.of(error)
673	        }
674	        return templates.map { template in
675	            let bytes = (try? Data(contentsOf: template.url)) ?? Data()
676	            if let refused = refused {
677	                return Entry(template: template, entry: .failed(refused, revision: ""))
678	            }
679	            let file = GraphicModuleFile(
680	                name: template.name, url: template.url, bytes: bytes, revision: "")
681	            return Entry(template: template, entry: GraphicRegistry.compile(file, library: library))
682	        }
683	    }
684	}

907	    /// Throws, writing nothing, when the file cannot be read or is not

910	        guard let store = graphicStore else {
911	            throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
912	        }
913	        let bytes: Data
914	        do {
915	            bytes = try Data(contentsOf: url)
916	        } catch {
917	            throw ReelCoreError(
918	                message: "\(url.path) could not be read: \(error.localizedDescription)")
919	        }
920	        guard let source = String(data: bytes, encoding: .utf8) else {
921	            throw ReelCoreError(

923	                    + "JavaScript")

926	            GraphicTemplates.moduleName(from: url.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent))

936	    /// when a duration or side is not a whole number in range.
937	    func graphicClipMaker(named name: String) throws -> (UInt32, Ticks) -> ReelOp {
938	        guard let store = graphicStore else {
939	            throw ReelCoreError(message: Self.noGraphicsFolderSentence)
940	        }

947	            let line = first?.line.map { " (line \($0))" } ?? ""

950	                    + (first?.message ?? "no diagnostic") + line)

969	                track: track, at: at, duration: duration, name: name, width: width,
970	                height: height, props: nil, schema: schema)

content.content:
//! A graphic clip's own timeline (road map 10's G-9) and the layer source
//! the recipe publishes for one (spec §7.3).
//!
//! A graphic has a timeline of its own, counted in the graphic's frames:
//! the clip's first frame shows graphic time `in`, and the graphic runs for
//! `length` ticks, or — `length` null — until the clip ends, which is
//! graphic time `in + duration` (decision G-9·c). The module is asked for
//! one frame of that timeline, with a `ctx` saying where the frame falls in
//! the whole, and returns SVG; the app rasterizes it and caches the texture
//! by the `hash` published here.
//!
//! The arithmetic lives here, in ONE place, because it has writers and a
//! reader that must agree on it: `trim_start`, `roll`, `split`'s second
//! half and `add_transition`'s head move `in` through [`graphic_advanced`],
//! `split` pins both halves' `length` to [`effective_length`], every
//! re-snap through `frame_grid.rs` puts `in` and `length` on the new grid
//! through [`graphic_resnapped`] (G-18), and the recipe reads the same
//! [`effective_length`] for `durationInFrames`. An edit module importing a
//! read-side one has precedent (`edit_split.rs` reads `actions` and
//! `source_window`); the two natural homes, `model_graphic.rs` and
//! `source_window.rs`, stand at their caps.
//!
//! The `ctx` keys are exactly the engine's (road map 10 §5c) and the app
//! passes the object through verbatim, so a key renamed here is a key the
//! module never sees. The core never names the engine's crate (G-2), so the
//! shape is restated, and `core/tests/graphic.rs` holds it to a fixture.

use serde_json::{Map, Value};

use crate::actions::Evaluated;
use crate::evaluate::number;
use crate::model::{Canvas, Clip, GraphicProps, Project};
use crate::recipe::{content_hash, missing_source};
use crate::source_window::in_advanced;
use crate::time::{frame_index, snap_down_to_frame, snap_up_to_frame, Ticks};

/// How long a graphic clip's own timeline is, in ticks, or `None` for a
/// clip that describes no graphic.
///

/// would make a front trim shorten the graphic's timeline and finish its
/// outro early while the clip still showed it (decision G-9·c). Under this
/// rule a front trim and a roll leave `durationInFrames` where it was.
pub(crate) fn effective_length(clip: &Clip) -> Option<Ticks> {
    clip.graphic.as_ref().map(|graphic| {
        graphic

            .unwrap_or(graphic.r#in.saturating_add(clip.duration))

}

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "What a graphic is"
description: "How a motion graphic works in Frame Job: a small module kept in your project that draws each frame, the clips it draws, and what its limits are."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A graphic is a motion graphic, such as a lower third, a chart or a countdown, drawn fresh on every frame by a small JavaScript module kept inside your project. You change what it shows with ordinary controls in the inspector, and you don't need to touch any code unless you want to.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder']}
  tools={['insert_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07-clip-graphic.window"
  alt="The editor with a clip called Graphic selected on the timeline, marked with curly braces. A lower third reading Jane Doe, Director of Photography sits at the bottom left of the preview, and the inspector's Graphic sub-tab lists its properties: Title, subtitle, accent, size, boxed and align."
/>

## Graphic clips

A graphic clip sits on a track like any other clip, and the graphic is the clip's content. It isn't an effect you apply to another clip, and it isn't a video or image file.

Frame Job comes with 23 [ready-made graphics](/graphics/templates/). You can also bring in a module of your own, [write one](/graphics/write-a-module/), or have [an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) write one. To put one on the timeline, see [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

A graphic is drawn at its own size, not stretched from a fixed picture. Change that size in the [Size section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) and text and shapes redraw sharply. Scaling the clip in the **Picture** sub-tab is different: that scales the picture already drawn.

## Modules

A module is one file, `graphics/<name>.js`, in your project. It draws a picture, as SVG, for any frame Frame Job asks for.

A module runs shut off from the outside world. It can't reach the network or the clock, and the only random numbers it can use are its own seeded ones. It also can't see the fonts installed on your Mac: graphics draw only with the fonts that come with Frame Job and the ones you [add to the project](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/), so a project draws the same on any Mac.

## Module names

A module's name is its file name without `.js`, such as `lower-third` or `title-2`. A name can use lowercase letters, digits and `-`, must start with a letter or a digit, and can be up to 63 characters long.

Frame Job skips a `.js` file in the folder with any other name, and the clip's [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/) warns about it.

## Typed properties

A module declares the properties it takes, and the inspector turns each one into a control. A property is a number, a true-or-false setting, a colour, a choice from a menu, text or a picture. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for each type's control.

A value you don't set draws with the module's own default. Like other clip settings, properties can change over time: see [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

Many clips can be drawn by one module. Each clip keeps its own property values, its own size and its own [timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/), so one lower third module can show a different name on every clip.

## Same frame, same pixels

A graphic always draws the same pixels for the same frame. What it draws depends only on the frame, the clip's size and timing, its property values, and the fonts and pictures it uses, so the preview and an export show the same graphic. There's no clock or outside randomness to make it differ between runs.

## Gradients don't band

Graphics are drawn in 256 levels per colour. Where a gradient has to round to those levels, Frame Job adds a fixed, very fine pattern of less than half a level, so a dark gradient shades smoothly instead of in steps. The pattern depends only on the pixel's position, so it doesn't crawl from frame to frame. Flat colours, pictures, text and transparency are drawn exactly, and there's nothing to set.

What happens to the pattern depends on where the frame ends up:

| Output | The gradient |
| --- | --- |
| **Save Frame…** and ProRes | The pattern survives, so the gradient stays smooth. |
| **HEVC 10-bit** | Most of the pattern is smoothed away, but the in-between shades stay, so the gradient stays smooth. |
| 8-bit H.264 or HEVC | The pattern is smoothed away too, and the steps come back. |

If a dark gradient matters, deliver at 10 bits or in ProRes. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/).

## The graphics folder

Each project keeps its graphics in a `graphics` folder inside the `.framejob` package. To see it, select a graphic clip and choose **Reveal in Finder** in the [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/).

| In the folder | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<name>.js` | The modules |
| `fonts/` | Fonts [added to the project](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) |
| `assets/` | Pictures added to the project |
| `history/` | [Earlier versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/) of each module, which you should leave to Frame Job |
| `API.md`, `API.d.ts` | The reference and its type definitions, for an editor or an agent working in the folder |

Frame Job creates the folder the first time something is written to it, so opening a project never adds one. Every save carries the folder, autosave included.

The folder holds files, not edits. A change to a file in it lands at once, isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited.

## Graphics in an untitled project

An unsaved project can use graphics. They're kept in a temporary folder and move into the package when you first save. If that folder is empty, the save doesn't create one in the package.

An untitled project restored from autosave gets its graphics back. Otherwise the temporary folder is removed when the window closes, so close an untitled project without saving and its graphics go with it.

## Templates are copied in

Inserting a [bundled template](/graphics/templates/) writes your own editable copy into the project's `graphics` folder, under a free name. The first Lower third is `lower-third`, the next `lower-third-2`, and so on. Each insert makes a new copy, so an existing graphic is never overwritten and each copy can be edited on its own. Two copies with one title are listed under **This Project** as "Lower third — lower-third" and "Lower third — lower-third-2".

Undo removes the clip, but not the copied file. To use one copy on several clips, [insert it from This Project](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/#insert-from-this-project), which copies nothing.

## A graphics-only timeline

A timeline of nothing but graphics, text, shapes and images still plays and exports. It doesn't need a video clip, and there's nothing to set.

## Graphics in HDR projects

In an HDR (HLG) project, graphics are drawn at HDR reference white, 203 cd/m², like titles and shapes. A white graphic matches SDR white and doesn't reach into the highlights. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

## Limits

- A graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
- A clip stores at most 64 property values.
- The **Properties** section shows only when all the selected clips share one module, and **Timeline** only for a single clip.
- Each frame has 250 ms to draw in the preview and 2 s in an export.
- **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** is unavailable while a nest is open.
- **File ▸ Delete Graphic…** won't delete a module while any clip uses it, including a clip inside a nest.
- Only the last 10 versions of each module are kept.
- Frame Job watches the first 16 module, font and picture files one by one. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for what that means in a bigger folder.
- The frames Frame Job holds in memory use at most a quarter of your Mac's memory, and less when memory is short. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## Related

- [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/)
- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)

---
title: "Insert a graphic"
description: "Pick a bundled template, a graphic already in your project or a file of your own, preview it, and place it at the playhead."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

**Insert ▸ Graphic…** is where you put a motion graphic on the timeline. You can pick one of the 23 bundled templates, a graphic already in your project, or a file of your own, and watch it play before you place it.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
  tools={['list_graphics', 'insert_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'render_graphic', 'write_graphic', 'import_graphic']}
/>

<Shot
  name="15e-graphic-browser-sheet.sheet"
  alt="The Insert Graphic sheet. On the left, the categories This Project, Data & Time, Screencast, Social & YouTube and Titles & Text. In the middle, the list of graphics, with Lower third chosen. On the right, the lower third plays over a checkerboard, with its title and the line A name and a subtitle sliding in on a bar under it. The bottom bar has Export… and From File… at the left, and Cancel and Insert at the right."
/>

## Insert a graphic

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to where the graphic should start.

2. Choose **Insert ▸ Graphic…**. The item has no keyboard shortcut, and it's greyed until the project's window is open.

3. Choose a category on the left, then a graphic in the middle. The preview on the right plays it.

4. Choose **Insert**, press <kbd>Return</kbd>, or double-click the graphic in the list.

</Steps>

Frame Job places the clip, selects it and closes the sheet. The inspector's **Clip** tab shows the new clip on its [**Graphic** sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/), ready for you to fill in.

Placing the clip is one undo step, **Insert Graphic**. If the graphic was a template, Frame Job first copied it into your project, and undo leaves that file where it is. See [Templates are copied in](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#templates-are-copied-in).

**Cancel** or <kbd>Esc</kbd> closes the sheet and changes nothing.

## The Insert Graphic sheet

The sheet has three panes, over a message line. The bottom bar has **Export…** and **From File…** at the left, and **Cancel** and **Insert** at the right. It opens on the first category's first graphic.

**Insert** is dimmed when no graphic is chosen. **Export…** saves the chosen graphic to give to someone else: see [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).

### Categories

The left list files the graphics by category. **This Project** comes first when your project holds a module, then the bundled categories in alphabetical order:

- **Data & Time**
- **Screencast**
- **Social & YouTube**
- **Titles & Text**

**This Project** lists every module in the project's `graphics` folder. A module of your own always appears there, whatever category it names for itself, and never in a bundled category. [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) lists what's in each category.

### The graphics list

The middle list shows the chosen category's graphics, sorted by title. A title comes from the module's own name for itself. Without one, Frame Job makes a title from the file name, so `lower-third` becomes Lower Third.

When two graphics under **This Project** share a title, each shows its module name as well, as in "Lower third — lower-third-2".

A module that doesn't compile is still listed, in grey, so you can see it's there and find out why it won't insert.

### The looping preview

The chosen graphic plays on a loop over a checkerboard, so you can see what's transparent. The preview has your project's canvas shape, and the graphic's title and a one-line description sit under it. Hold the pointer over a description that's cut off to read all of it.

The preview uses the graphic's default properties, at the project's frame rate. A slow graphic skips frames rather than falling behind. A module that fails shows its red error card here.

## Insert from This Project

Choosing a graphic under **This Project** places another clip drawn by that module, as it is. Nothing is copied, so this is how you use one graphic on several clips. Each clip keeps its own property values, but editing the module changes every clip it draws. See [Clips sharing one module](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#clips-sharing-one-module).

## Insert from a file

<Steps>

1. Choose **From File…**. The sheet closes and a file panel opens.

2. Choose a `.js` module, or a `.fjgraphic` package.

</Steps>

Frame Job copies a `.js` file into the project under a [new name](#how-the-module-is-named) and places a clip drawn by it, as **Insert** does. The file must be UTF-8 text. If it isn't, Frame Job says so and copies nothing.

A `.fjgraphic` package doesn't go straight in. Frame Job shows you what's in it and asks first: see [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/).

### How the module is named

The module is named after the file you chose, made into a legal, free [module name](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/#module-names):

1. The name is lowercased.
2. Each run of anything other than a to z and 0 to 9 becomes one `-`.
3. Dashes are trimmed from the ends.
4. The result is cut to 60 characters. If nothing is left, the name is `graphic`.
5. If that name is taken, it gets `-2`, `-3` and so on.

So `My Title.js` becomes `my-title`, and `My Counter (v2).js` becomes `my-counter-v2`.

## Where it lands

A new graphic starts at the playhead, on the front track if there's room for it. If there isn't, it goes on a new track above everything. [Adding a text clip](/text-and-shapes/text-clips/) follows the same rule.

With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the clip goes on the nest's front track, or on a new track inside the nest.

## Default length and size

A module can give its own length and size. Otherwise the clip is 5 seconds long and the size of the canvas.

A module gives its length in frames, counted at the project's frame rate, so a 150-frame graphic lasts 5 seconds at 30 fps and 2.5 seconds at 60 fps. [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) lists each template's length. You can change the length and size afterwards: see [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/).

A graphic bigger than the canvas is scaled down to fit when **Fit new clips to canvas** is on in the [Document tab](/projects/document-tab/), as a shape is. It still draws at its own size.

Frame Job won't place a clip when the module's length isn't a whole number of at least 1 frame, or its width or height isn't a whole number from 1 to 8192. The message names the value that's wrong.

## A module that doesn't compile

If the module doesn't compile, no clip is placed. Frame Job beeps and tells you the first error, and the line it's on when it knows:

> `graphics/<name>.js does not compile: <message> (line N)`

From the sheet, the message appears under the lists and the sheet stays open. **From File…** shows it in an alert.

A copy Frame Job made along the way stays in your project, whether it came from a template or a file. You'll find it in grey under **This Project**. Fix it and insert it from there, or remove it with [**File ▸ Delete Graphic…**](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

Anything else that stops an insert appears in the same message line, word for word, and the sheet stays open.

## On the timeline

A graphic clip is teal and has no thumbnails. Its strip shows a `{}` symbol and reads **Graphic**, until you [give it a name](/timeline/names-and-labels/). The block under the timeline and the inspector's clip header call it a graphic.

## Good to know

The sheet reads what's in your project when it opens. A module you add while it's open appears the next time you open it.

## With an agent

An agent can list what the sheet offers and insert a graphic at the playhead, as you can. It can also do two things the sheet can't: look at a module without placing a clip, and place a clip on the track and at the time it chooses, with its own length, size and property values. See [Tools: graphics](/mcp/tools-graphics/) and [Graphics with an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/).

## Related

- [What a graphic is](/graphics/what-is-a-graphic/)
- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
- [Share a graphic](/graphics/share-a-graphic/)

A graphic clip is teal and has no thumbnails. Its strip shows a `{}` symbol and reads **Graphic**, until you [give it a name](/timeline/names-and-labels/). The block under the timeline and the inspector's clip header call it a graphic.

## Good to know

The sheet reads what's in your project when it opens. A module you add while it's open appears the next time you open it.

## With an agent

An agent can list what the sheet offers and insert a graphic at the playhead, as you can. It can also do two things the sheet can't: look at a module without placing a clip, and place a clip on the track and at the time it chooses, with its own length, size and property values. ---
title: "What a graphic is"
description: "How a motion graphic works in Frame Job: a small module kept in your project that draws each frame, the clips it draws, and what its limits are."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A graphic is a motion graphic, such as a lower third, a chart or a countdown, drawn fresh on every frame by a small JavaScript module kept inside your project. You change what it shows with ordinary controls in the inspector, and you don't need to touch any code unless you want to.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Insert ▸ Graphic…"
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Source ▸ Reveal in Finder']}
  tools={['insert_graphic', 'add_graphic_clip', 'write_graphic', 'get_graphic']}
/>

<Shot
  name="07-clip-graphic.window"
  alt="The editor with a clip called Graphic selected on the timeline, marked with curly braces. A lower third reading Jane Doe, Director of Photography sits at the bottom left of the preview, and the inspector's Graphic sub-tab lists its properties: Title, subtitle, accent, size, boxed and align."
/>

## Graphic clips

A graphic clip sits on a track like any other clip, and the graphic is the clip's content. It isn't an effect you apply to another clip, and it isn't a video or image file.

Frame Job comes with 23 [ready-made graphics](/graphics/templates/). You can also bring in a module of your own, [write one](/graphics/write-a-module/), or have [an agent](/graphics/agents-and-graphics/) write one. To put one on the timeline, see [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/).

A graphic is drawn at its own size, not stretched from a fixed picture. Change that size in the [Size section](/graphics/size-and-timing/) and text and shapes redraw sharply. Scaling the clip in the **Picture** sub-tab is different: that scales the picture already drawn.

## Modules

A module is one file, `graphics/<name>.js`, in your project. It draws a picture, as SVG, for any frame Frame Job asks for.

A module runs shut off from the outside world. It can't reach the network or the clock, and the only random numbers it can use are its own seeded ones. It also can't see the fonts installed on your Mac: graphics draw only with the fonts that come with Frame Job and the ones you [add to the project](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/), so a project draws the same on any Mac.

## Module names

A module's name is its file name without `.js`, such as `lower-third` or `title-2`. A name can use lowercase letters, digits and `-`, must start with a letter or a digit, and can be up to 63 characters long.

Frame Job skips a `.js` file in the folder with any other name, and the clip's [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/) warns about it.

## Typed properties

A module declares the properties it takes, and the inspector turns each one into a control. A property is a number, a true-or-false setting, a colour, a choice from a menu, text or a picture. See [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/) for each type's control.

A value you don't set draws with the module's own default. Like other clip settings, properties can change over time: see [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/).

## Clips sharing one module

Many clips can be drawn by one module. Each clip keeps its own property values, its own size and its own [timeline](/graphics/size-and-timing/), so one lower third module can show a different name on every clip.

Editing the module changes every clip it draws. To change one clip's look alone, select it and choose **Duplicate as New Graphic…** in the [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/), which gives it a copy of the module to itself.

## Same frame, same pixels

A graphic always draws the same pixels for the same frame. What it draws depends only on the frame, the clip's size and timing, its property values, and the fonts and pictures it uses, so the preview and an export show the same graphic. There's no clock or outside randomness to make it differ between runs.

## Gradients don't band

Graphics are drawn in 256 levels per colour. Where a gradient has to round to those levels, Frame Job adds a fixed, very fine pattern of less than half a level, so a dark gradient shades smoothly instead of in steps. The pattern depends only on the pixel's position, so it doesn't crawl from frame to frame. Flat colours, pictures, text and transparency are drawn exactly, and there's nothing to set.

What happens to the pattern depends on where the frame ends up:

| Output | The gradient |
| --- | --- |
| **Save Frame…** and ProRes | The pattern survives, so the gradient stays smooth. |
| **HEVC 10-bit** | Most of the pattern is smoothed away, but the in-between shades stay, so the gradient stays smooth. |
| 8-bit H.264 or HEVC | The pattern is smoothed away too, and the steps come back. |

If a dark gradient matters, deliver at 10 bits or in ProRes. See [Export bit depth](/export/bit-depth/).

## The graphics folder

Each project keeps its graphics in a `graphics` folder inside the `.framejob` package. To see it, select a graphic clip and choose **Reveal in Finder** in the [Source section](/graphics/graphic-tab/).

| In the folder | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `<name>.js` | The modules |
| `fonts/` | Fonts [added to the project](/graphics/fonts-and-pictures/) |
| `assets/` | Pictures added to the project |
| `history/` | [Earlier versions](/graphics/edit-a-module/) of each module, which you should leave to Frame Job |
| `API.md`, `API.d.ts` | The reference and its type definitions, for an editor or an agent working in the folder |

Frame Job creates the folder the first time something is written to it, so opening a project never adds one. Every save carries the folder, autosave included.

The folder holds files, not edits. A change to a file in it lands at once, isn't an undo step and doesn't mark the project as edited.

## Graphics in an untitled project

An unsaved project can use graphics. They're kept in a temporary folder and move into the package when you first save. If that folder is empty, the save doesn't create one in the package.

An untitled project restored from autosave gets its graphics back. Otherwise the temporary folder is removed when the window closes, so close an untitled project without saving and its graphics go with it.

## Templates are copied in

Inserting a [bundled template](/graphics/templates/) writes your own editable copy into the project's `graphics` folder, under a free name. The first Lower third is `lower-third`, the next `lower-third-2`, and so on. Each insert makes a new copy, so an existing graphic is never overwritten and each copy can be edited on its own. Two copies with one title are listed under **This Project** as "Lower third — lower-third" and "Lower third — lower-third-2".

Undo removes the clip, but not the copied file. To use one copy on several clips, [insert it from This Project](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/#insert-from-this-project), which copies nothing.

## A graphics-only timeline

A timeline of nothing but graphics, text, shapes and images still plays and exports. It doesn't need a video clip, and there's nothing to set.

## Graphics in HDR projects

In an HDR (HLG) project, graphics are drawn at HDR reference white, 203 cd/m², like titles and shapes. A white graphic matches SDR white and doesn't reach into the highlights. See [A project's dynamic range](/hdr/dynamic-range/).

## Limits

- A graphic draws at most 8192 pixels on a side.
- A clip stores at most 64 property values.
- The **Properties** section shows only when all the selected clips share one module, and **Timeline** only for a single clip.
- Each frame has 250 ms to draw in the preview and 2 s in an export.
- **File ▸ Rename Graphic…** is unavailable while a nest is open.
- **File ▸ Delete Graphic…** won't delete a module while any clip uses it, including a clip inside a nest.
- Only the last 10 versions of each module are kept.
- Frame Job watches the first 16 module, font and picture files one by one. See [Edit a module](/graphics/edit-a-module/) for what that means in a bigger folder.
- The frames Frame Job holds in memory use at most a quarter of your Mac's memory, and less when memory is short. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

## Related

- [Insert a graphic](/graphics/insert-a-graphic/)
- [Bundled templates](/graphics/templates/)
- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)

If the module doesn't compile, no clip is placed. Frame Job beeps and tells you the first error, and the line it's on when it knows:

> `graphics/<name>.js does not compile: <message> (line N)`

From the sheet, the message appears under the lists and the sheet stays open. **From File…** shows it in an alert.

A copy Frame Job made along the way stays in your project, whether it came from a template or a file. You'll find it in grey under **This Project**. Fix it and insert it from there, or remove it with [**File ▸ Delete Graphic…**](/graphics/manage-graphics/).

Anything else that stops an insert appears in the same message line, word for word, and the sheet stays open.
